Requested by claude-klabauter-em (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-06-claude-klabauter-em-declare-reaped-from-session-in-canonical-handoff-schema.md); engine half already landed there (4581f7bf6, b9803ea41) writing the field against a canonical schema that did not declare it, and claude-klabauter deliberately did NOT hand-edit its vendored copy, which is the correct call — a local edit manufactures exactly the divergence schema_drift_watch.py exists to catch. Classified nested-field-additive, NOT major, per schema-version-gate.md § Bump-class extension key's own vocabulary table: a new OPTIONAL top-level scalar on the existing handoff entity, narrowing no declared domain and invalidating no existing document. The sender's read is adopted unchanged. The `major` reading it feared came from the 2.4.0 -> 2.5.0 entry below, which declared the structurally-identical `gate_cleared_by` and IS classed major — but that bump earned major from a DIFFERENT change bundled into it (a `pattern` constraint added to `blocked_by`'s previously-unconstrained items), not from the declaration; the most restrictive bundled class governs the whole commit, so that entry is no precedent for classing a standalone declaration major. Reader-first is satisfied in substance rather than in sequence here — the consumer is the requester and is already ahead, writing the field; there is no reader to widen first, only a vendored copy to re-sync. handoff-archived.schema.json takes the SAME declaration in this same commit (its own 2.3.0 -> 2.4.0, same class): the sender explicitly asserted nothing about the archived twin and reverted a backfill that reached into archived records, correctly, since writing the key onto archived documents asserts a conclusion about them. Declaring it there asserts no such thing — the archival path carries frontmatter through wholesale, so a live carrier archives carrying it, and the archive schema already declares the whole claim vocabulary (consumed_by/consumed_at/claimed_by/claimed_at) this field sits beside. Leaving it undeclared there would rebuild, one archival sweep later, precisely the undeclared-on-disk state this bump exists to end. PRIOR: 5.0.0 -> 6.0.0 (deliverable-id-pattern) constrains the STRING arm of `deliverable_id` with `^dlv-(?!placeholder-replace-with)[0-9a-zA-Z][0-9a-zA-Z.-]*$` — the `null` arm is untouched (null is the documented pre-backfill value; 10 live records in this repo rely on it). Classified MAJOR by the identical reasoning as the entries below: constraining a declared domain, no carve-out. It is not record-validating -- no handoff frontmatter ever carries a `baton_class` key, so no consumer's per-record shape validation is affected by this bump -- but the pin gate hashes the whole schema file body regardless of whether a key sits under `properties`, so the bump is still required to keep the content-hash pin honest. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-29-baton-kind-vocabulary-one-axis-per-field.md § D1/D2. 2.6.0 -> 3.0.0 (spike-verdict-records-stable-evidence-home C3) removed the `spike-result` value from both the top-level `kinds` enumeration and the per-record `kind` enum, and struck the spike-result clause from `kind`'s description prose. Structurally: `covers_prose`+`legs[]` required-together inside the object; each leg is `propertyNames`-blocked from carrying the four resolver-only keys (`read_ok`/`observed`/`error`/`elapsed`) so an author cannot free their own gate (ratification Finding 2); a record-level `allOf` over `legs.items` pins `ref`/`repo`/`expected`/`reason`/`note` shape per one of nine closed-enum `kind` values, mirroring cutover.schema.json's `confirmed_consumers[].verified_by` allOf pattern. x-baton-class.description: DERIVED-field lookup (D2) -- baton_class is NEVER written to on-disk frontmatter; a consuming function computes it on read by indexing this map with the record's own `kind` value: `x_baton_class['mapping'][record['kind']]`. Direction chosen deliberately as kind -> class, not class -> kinds: the caller of this derivation always already holds a record with a `kind` value in hand and wants its class, which is a direct O(1) lookup in this direction; the inverse (class -> kinds) would force every caller to build its own inverted index from this same data before it could answer the question it actually has. Three classes, closed set: continuation (session-handoff, recovery), deflection (spinoff, goal-seed), intention (roadmap-baton, roadmap-seed) -- see docs/plans/2026-07-29-baton-kind-vocabulary-one-axis-per-field.md § D2 for the axis rationale. The `mapping` below names the D1 TARGET names (goal-seed, roadmap-baton, roadmap-seed) -- the C10 enum narrow that admits them into this schema's own `kinds` array and `properties.kind.enum` above (retiring spinoff-goal/spinoff-roadmap/spinoff-roadmap-creator) has landed as of the 3.1.0 -> 4.0.0 bump below. A schema-parity test (coordinator/tests/) asserts every kind named here is a member of the known-kind universe (union of `kinds`/`properties.kind.enum` and this migration's D1 target table), that every class is one of the three above, and that no kind is double-assigned. `recovery` is retained per C1a's KEEP disposition (state/plan-sidecars/2026-07-29-baton-kind-vocabulary.recovery-disposition.md) rather than struck as a dead value. If a genuinely separate artifact is ever wanted for another tool's consumption (e.g. Example-retrieval-repo), it MUST be GENERATED from this mapping with its own parity test against this key -- never hand-authored independently, which is exactly the two-sources-of-truth drift this migration exists to close.

description: Active handoff baton — carries session-continuation state for /pickup and workstream tracking. Cross-field rules (deployment_state gates, graph-primitive kind-gate, category/summary cutoff, spinoff-with-predecessor, supersedes kind-gate, handoff_phase stamp-required-when-execution, handoff_phase kind-gate) live in CROSS_FIELD_RULES['handoff'] in bin/lib/schema.js and are applied automatically by validateRecord. Origin-axis rules (kind-prefixed id well-formedness, per-kind cardinality, direct self-reference rejection, predecessor:none invariant for spinoff kinds, forked_from/origin_handoff never-silently-disagree invariant) are also in CROSS_FIELD_RULES['handoff'] (C2). Backfill policy: pre-existing forks carry null for all origin_* fields; no migration. Record-level provenance (ProvenanceEnvelope — how the pipeline observed/derived this record) is DISTINCT from artifact-level origin_* (what spawned this fork) — same word, different plane; origin_* stays frontmatter-only and is not projected into the ProvenanceEnvelope. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-07-spinoff-provenance-ancestry.md § Field shape

branch.description: Git branch this handoff was created on.

status.description: Lifecycle state. DR-084 P4 narrow landed 2026-07-22: old values 'active'/'consumed' retired, only 'open'/'claimed' admitted. 'superseded' is retired (2026-06-26).

predecessor.description: Predecessor handoff path, or null/"none" for spinoffs. Key must always be present (string-or-null, D9 nullable rule).

predecessor_id.description: ID-companion for predecessor (C2, add-not-swap) — the predecessor's handoff_id, resolved and stamped at author time from the SAME predecessor the path field names (never a different one; the adjacency-inference ban is unaffected). Path-independent, survives predecessor archival/rename — the mechanism a machine walks; predecessor remains the human-legible display string. Null when the predecessor has no handoff_id (pre-existing artifact, no backfill) or predecessor is none/null. Never-silently-disagree cross-field rule (predecessor/predecessor_id must resolve to the same artifact when both non-null) is owned by C3, not this schema file. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-08-lifecycle-vocab-c2-durable-links-rollup.md § C2

consumed_by.description: Session id of the consuming /pickup invocation; sourced from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID with .current-session-id fallback.

consumed_at.description: Timestamp when the handoff was consumed (ISO 8601 date-time). Stamped by cs_consume_handoff for race-forensics precision.

claimed_by.description: Session id of the claiming /pickup invocation (DR-084 successor of consumed_by; new-vocabulary records use this). Sourced from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID with .current-session-id fallback. Cross-field rule (claimed + claimed_at ⇒ claimed_by required) lands at P4.

claimed_at.description: Timestamp when the handoff was claimed (ISO 8601 date-time; DR-084 successor of consumed_at). Stamped by the claim transition for race-forensics precision.

reaped_from_session.description: Session id of the DEAD holder whose claim a crash-orphan reaper released, preserved at strip time so the fact of prior consumption survives the strip. Written by claude-klabauter's `_unclaim` inside the same mutate closure that removes the claim vocabulary (claimed_by/claimed_at/consumed_by/consumed_at) — a second write would reproduce the bug it fixes on a crash between the two. Distinct from claimed_by: claimed_by names the LIVE holder, reaped_from_session names a holder already gone. Its presence is forensic provenance ONLY and asserts nothing about completion — a reaped baton re-advertises as available work, and nothing here proves that work was finished (claude-klabauter's drift sweep surfaces the population in a `reaped_orphan` bucket and deliberately never closes one). Absent on every baton that was never reaped.

machine.description: Machine identifier (host name) where the session ran.

kind.description: Handoff kind. Cross-field rules enforce kind-specific constraints (graph primitives require roadmap-baton, supersedes requires spinoff, spinoff/goal-seed/roadmap-seed requires predecessor=none/null). recovery: requires predecessor: <crashed-sha> or null (no cross-field rule enforced, convention only).

authoring_session.description: Session id that authored this handoff. Required by convention on spinoffs as audit trail back to origin. On kind: session-handoff, coordinator-doc-new's scaffolder stamps this machine-generated at scaffold time (omitted, not PLACEHOLDER, when no session id is resolvable) -- coordinator_core.baton_assemble's cross-authorship adoption predicate (_adopt_prior_attempt_scaffold_path) gates adoption of a prior attempt's scaffold on this field matching the resuming run's own session id.

workstream.description: Short slug grouping related forks. Required by convention on spinoffs.

repo.description: Repo id for install-leg spinoff batons (kind: spinoff seeded by a downstream installer).

install_chain_order.description: Relative install position for install-leg spinoffs (lower = earlier; coordinator = 0).

pickup_ready.description: Positive pickup-authorized signal. Absence triggers a non-blocking warning at /pickup time.

deployment_state.description: Lifecycle readiness state. DR-084 P4 narrow landed 2026-07-22: 'abandoned' retired; 'continued' (succession terminal) and 'closed' (deliberate stop, human/session only) are its replacements. Conditional-required coupling (continued→continued_into, closed→closed_reason) also lands at this narrow. Existing cross-field rules unchanged: awaiting_gate→gate_dependency required; ready_to_fire→gate_dependency forbidden; shipped→shipped_in required (post-cutoff).

gate_dependency.description: DEPRECATED (C2) — superseded by blocked_by/no_longer_blocked_by/gate_cleared_by, which admit handoff_id values alongside stub_id and give the gate a resolvable index instead of a free-text one-liner. Old values retired in spirit, not schema-enforced-retired: existing awaiting_gate records still populate this field and it remains shape-valid, but new authoring should prefer blocked_by. NO LONGER UNCONDITIONALLY REQUIRED (C3): an awaiting_gate record must carry AT LEAST ONE of gate_dependency, non-empty blocked_by, or non-empty blocking_notes — a record with none of the three still fails. That three-way OR is enforced in the Python cross-field layer only (H-CROSS-1), NOT in this file's allOf, which encodes just the ready_to_fire-forbids-gate_dependency twin; stated here so a schema-only reader is not misled. Path-shaped values are now REJECTED (C2b, H-CROSS-9): a value containing 'tasks/' or 'archive/', or ending '.md', fails validation — put the baton dependency in blocked_by as a slug and any advisory prose in blocking_notes. Formerly: 'Required when deployment_state=awaiting_gate. One-liner naming the subsystem or condition that gates this handoff. Must be subsystem-named, not file-pathed.'

no_longer_blocked_by.description: Predecessors verified shipped — entries MOVE here from blocked_by (never dropped): a resolution relocates one blocked_by entry into no_longer_blocked_by, it does not delete it from either array. The union of blocked_by and no_longer_blocked_by is invariant across a resolution — same total membership, entries just migrate columns as their blockers clear. Same slug shape as blocked_by (stub_id or handoff_id).

blocking_notes.description: Advisory prose, NEVER read by the resolver — inert by construction. Home for the 'needs a Windows box' class of real-but-not-a-dependency constraint: true and worth recording, but not a blocked_by/no_longer_blocked_by entry because nothing on the graph clears it. Do not encode anything here that the resolver is meant to act on — that belongs in blocked_by.

gate_cleared_by.description: SHA provenance — which commit(s) discharged the gate. Written by _gate_cascade_clear; previously drifted onto disk undeclared (no additionalProperties:false to catch it) before this schema named it. Distinct from no_longer_blocked_by: gate_cleared_by answers 'which commit discharged the gate', no_longer_blocked_by answers 'which baton used to block' (slug history, not commit provenance). Both ship — they answer different questions, neither substitutes for the other.

gate_evidence.description: Structured, machine-checkable evidence for a prose gate_dependency/blocked_by sentence -- the ratified declaration half of the C6 external-gate-evidence vocabulary (consumer already landed at claude-klabauter coordinator_core/reconcile/gate_eval.py, commit 7e69ecc1; this is what a caller assembles for it to read). Spec backlink: state/plan-sidecars/2026-07-27-gate-resolution-widen-and-migrate.c6-witness-set-ratification.md (the Director of Engineering, eng-director) -- that ratification is authoritative over the landed evaluator wherever the two disagree; the amendments below are rework on already-landed code, not a free authoring choice (Finding 1). A NEW witness source feeding evaluate_gate's existing clear/narrow/surface/not-cleared prose mechanism (rule 0, gated on covers_prose:true) -- never a fifth verdict class (Structural finding Part A). additionalProperties intentionally permissive, matching this file's convention elsewhere; the propertyNames guard below is the load-bearing restriction, not additionalProperties.

covers_prose.description: REQUIRED. Human assertion that legs[] fully cover what the prose gate_dependency/blocked_by sentence asserts. Checked FIRST by evaluate_gate's rule 0: only when this is explicitly true do the legs become authoritative and get AND-reduced onto the prose verdict; any other value (absent, or explicitly false) leaves prose dominant and every leg inert (D2a). This is not a partial-credit knob -- a record with covers_prose:false and a full legs[] array is valid and means 'these legs exist but do not yet fully discharge the prose sentence', a documented and expected shape for a partial backfill (three of C10's fifteen backfill targets are known to land here).

legs.description: REQUIRED, non-empty, FLAT array -- never nested. An empty legs[] is malformed and never vacuously frees the gate (the reducer treats it as indeterminate). Nesting was considered and rejected: it reintroduces a summary value that hides which half failed, the same last_gate_recheck vacuity this vocabulary exists to cure.

leg_id.description: REQUIRED. Stable per-leg identifier, unique within this record's legs[] -- enforced by cross-field/engine rule, not this JSON Schema (same division of labor as carried_items[].carry_id above: schema declares the field required, a cross-field gate enforces uniqueness). The landed evaluator defaults an absent leg_id to the literal string '<unknown>'; two defaulted legs would report identically and the flat list's entire reason for existing -- per-leg result attribution -- evaporates. Do not rely on that default.

kind.description: CLOSED ENUM discriminator selecting how repo/ref/expected/reason/note are shaped (record-level allOf below pins the per-kind shape) and which resolver predicate applies -- engine consumer: claude-klabauter coordinator_core/reconcile/gate_eval.py _evaluate_gate_evidence_leg. The first four names are carried VERBATIM from cutover.schema.json's confirmed_consumers[].verified_by.kind, but the SHAPE is not a verbatim carry-over: cutover resolves repo roots at the confirmed_consumers RECORD level from gate_source.repos[] and has no per-entry repo field, whereas gate_evidence has no record-level repo declaration at all, so repo: below is a genuine extension, not an inherited field (Finding 5). The next three are deliberately KEBAB-CASE (file-exists, frontmatter-field, commit-ancestor) even though the landed evaluator's own frozensets spell them snake_case (file_exists, frontmatter_field, commit_ancestor) -- kebab is the ratified authoring form (Finding 4: a mixed-casing discriminator is a live typo generator against a closed enum, and the ratification normalizes the newly-added five to kebab; deadline/human are single words and unaffected either way). Per-kind resolution: test-node-id -- a pytest node id the resolver re-runs; satisfied iff observed is True. probe-op-key -- an engine op-key the resolver re-invokes; satisfied iff observed is True. commit-sha -- a commit the resolver git-shows and pattern-matches; satisfied iff observed is True. sibling-commitment-ref -- an FK to a state/cross-repo-commitments/*.yaml record; satisfied iff observed is True. commit-ancestor -- distinct from commit-sha (ancestry, not content-match); the resolver runs git ancestry, satisfied iff observed is True; ref MUST name both ends (a bare SHA with an implicit default target is the same silent-wrong-tree failure the mandatory repo: rule exists to prevent). file-exists -- the resolver stats the path; satisfied iff observed == expected -- existence is never satisfaction (an artifact can exist and say nothing), so expected and note are both required on this kind alone, and where the checked artifact carries a machine-readable state field, frontmatter-field is mandatory instead and file-exists is inadmissible (an actioned cross-repo memo's real condition is status: actioned, not its presence in archive/). frontmatter-field -- the resolver reads the field; satisfied iff observed == expected -- the strongest of the four, converting 'the memo is actioned' into a machine fact. deadline -- no I/O: the resolver computes elapsed from the authored absolute ISO-8601 date carried in ref (never a relative expression); this is a PROMPT, not a satisfier, and is excluded from the AND-reduce toward freed. Three distinguishable signal classes exist and only this kind produces the middle one -- a leg that has been resolved, one that is merely aged with nothing left to re-derive (review-due), and one nobody has looked at yet -- never conflate these three. human -- declared-unresolvable by construction, always indeterminate; the honest alternative to prose that looks resolvable and never is. reason is REQUIRED non-empty here (the landed evaluator's own default of 'no reason authored' is explicitly not relied upon by this schema -- a reasonless human leg is a hiding place, not honest-indeterminate). An unrecognized kind value is schema-inadmissible by this closed enum; a pre-schema record reaching the evaluator with one is marked indeterminate exactly like a human leg, but the two are NOT the same fact -- one is a data defect this enum should have prevented, the other is deliberate declared indeterminacy -- and a triage report must be able to tell them apart (Finding 7).

repo.description: Registry key the leg resolves against (e.g. Example_doctrine_repo, claude_klabauter) -- NEVER a filesystem path. REQUIRED on every kind except human and deadline (ruling 6 / Finding 6) -- do not infer a leg's repo from context; a resolver that infers resolves against the wrong tree silently. An unregistered repo value resolves read_ok:false at the resolver, which this module's predicate maps to indeterminate, never unsatisfied -- mirroring cutover's fail-closed unscanned-foreign-repo clause. Genuine EXTENSION of cutover's verified_by shape, not a verbatim carry (Finding 5) -- see the kind description above.

ref.description: The evidence reference, shaped per kind (record-level allOf below enforces the pairing): a pytest node id (test-node-id), an invokable op-key (probe-op-key), a full or abbreviated commit SHA (commit-sha), a state/cross-repo-commitments/*.yaml filename, bare or path-qualified (sibling-commitment-ref), '<commit-ish>@<target-ref>' naming both ends -- never a bare SHA (commit-ancestor), a repo-relative path (file-exists), '<repo-relative-path>#<field-name>' (frontmatter-field), or an absolute ISO-8601 date, never a relative expression (deadline). NOT CARRIED on kind=human -- reason carries the entire justification there instead.

expected.description: Equality-kind comparand. REQUIRED and typed per-kind (record-level allOf below): boolean on file-exists; non-null scalar on frontmatter-field. Not applicable to the five boolean-observed kinds (test-node-id, probe-op-key, commit-sha, sibling-commitment-ref, commit-ancestor), to deadline (whose predicate is the resolver's own elapsed computation), or to human (never machine-resolved) -- none of those compare an observation against an authored expectation. A null or absent expected on frontmatter-field collapses that kind into file-exists and re-opens the existence-is-not-satisfaction trap file-exists's own required note exists to flag -- do not author it that way.

reason.description: REQUIRED non-empty on kind=human only -- the entire justification for the declared-unresolvable kind. This schema requires it structurally precisely because the landed evaluator's own fallback ('no reason authored') is not an acceptable authored value -- a covers_prose:true block containing any human leg can never reach freed, and reason is the only accountability a human leg carries. Free prose, never machine-compared against anything.

note.description: Commentary, NEVER machine-read by the resolver or the reducer -- on a corpus that just spent this whole plan learning that prose gates do not resolve, do not put the real condition here; it belongs in ref/expected. REQUIRED non-empty on kind=file-exists only, where it must state what the existence check actually proves. Optional free text on every other kind.

ref.description: '<commit-ish>@<target-ref>' -- the '@' is load-bearing: a bare SHA with no '@' fails this pattern outright, which is deliberate (a bare SHA implies an implicit default target and re-opens the silent-wrong-tree failure the mandatory repo: rule exists to prevent, per Finding 6).
'<repo-relative-path>#<field-name>' -- exactly one '#', non-empty on both sides.

expected.description: Non-null scalar, REQUIRED. A null or absent expected collapses this kind into file-exists and re-opens the existence-is-not-satisfaction trap (ruling 2).

ref.description: Absolute ISO-8601 date (or date-time), NEVER a relative expression ('in 2 weeks', '+7d'). elapsed is resolver-computed from this value and is authoring-forbidden (see the propertyNames guard on this object).

last_gate_recheck.description: Timestamp of the last gate-recheck pass; stamped by the gate-recheck verb regardless of --cleared.

park_note.description: Optional single-line note recorded by the unconsume transition when a picked-up baton is returned to the shelf (why it was un-consumed). Written by handoff-transition.js unconsume --note / cs_unconsume_handoff.

shipped_in.description: The commit at which this baton was declared shipped (a caller-supplied ship commit), always a resolvable SHA, OR the sanctioned substantively-shipped-no-commit:<YYYY-MM-DD> stealth-skip token. Any set value is shape-validated by this pattern unconditionally; the date-gated *requirement* to set shipped_in on shipped handoffs lives in cross-field Rule A3a-2b (pre-cutoff shipped handoffs predating the convention are exempt from the requirement, not from value shape). Companion field shipped_in_kind tags which of the sanctioned resolutions produced this value — read that field's description before assuming this is a direct ship commit. The caller-supplied ship commit is DR-096 meaning 2; see DR-096 for the full taxonomy of how this value is resolved.

shipped_in_kind.description: Discriminant for how shipped_in was resolved — required whenever shipped_in is set (required-when-shipped, alongside shipped_in itself). Makes the *meaning* of shipped_in type-checkable by this tag instead of by regex-sniffing the string it points at. ship-commit = the commit at which this baton was declared shipped (the canonical case: a caller-supplied ship commit at write time). successor = the SHA belongs to a successor or the deliverable that resolved this baton (handoff_reconcile gate-a); the successor pointer itself lives in the existing succession fields (continued_into / disposed_successors), NOT duplicated here — this only tags that shipped_in's SHA was sourced from that lineage, not a direct ship commit. scope-derived = legacy/best-effort resolution from the baton's own scope paths (retired as the PREFERRED write-time strategy per DR-096, not eliminated as a write path outright: three in-process sha-less stampers — wsc_commit.py's pre-commit tail, /update-docs Phase 8, and boot_sweep's best-effort stamp — can each still select this kind when no caller-supplied sha is available; none is reached via a CLI --sha flag. As of the 2026-07-26 blast-radius audit (state/audits/2026-07-26-scope-derived-retirement-blast-radius.md), this kind appears ZERO times on disk across either repo's live or archived corpus — a <24h observation window since shipped_in_kind started being written, not a durable absence proof. Retiring this write path is orthogonal to the handoff archival backlog, not a drain measure for it. See DR-096 § Current state vs. target state for the corrected account before assuming this tag never appears on a freshly-written value). no-commit = shipped_in holds the substantively-shipped-no-commit:<date> token, not a SHA.

continued_into.description: Successor pointer for deployment_state=continued — handoff_id (hnd-<slug>-<6hex>) preferred, state/handoffs/... path fallback (pre-existing successors carry no handoff_id; no backfill). The tooth that keeps 'continued' from becoming liveness-guess abandonment: an automated writer that cannot name the successor cannot stamp continued. Required-when-continued (landed at the P4 narrow, 2026-07-22).

disposed_successors.description: Lineage-preservation edges written by distill.apply_disposal (C14) BEFORE a successor handoff is deleted: each entry is a successor's continued-into value (handoff_id preferred, path fallback — same shape as continued_into) for a successor that continued this record's work and was later disposed by /distill. Multi-valued (unlike continued_into, single-valued and deployment_state=continued-gated) because a parent can accumulate multiple disposed successors across separate /distill runs; each entry is append-only and never overwritten. Distinct from continued_into: this field is NOT deployment_state-conditional and is NOT itself the successor pointer for this record's own lifecycle — it is a reverse-pointing lineage record of OTHER records that pointed at this one and have since been deleted.

closed_reason.description: Deliberate-stop subtype for deployment_state=closed (human/session only, never automated — DR-084). cancelled = deliberate stop; displaced = replaced with NO lineage edge (with an edge it's continued, not closed); stale = overtaken by events. Deliberately NO crashed/orphaned value: a successor-less dead-holder has no automated terminal — it surfaces for adjudication. Required-when-closed (landed at the P4 narrow, 2026-07-22).

blocks.description: Stub IDs this stub blocks. Permitted on ANY kind as of C1 — the former roadmap-only cross-field gate was removed so the gate resolver can carry non-roadmap batons. (kind=roadmap-baton still REQUIRES this field, along with roadmap_id/stub_id/wave/blocked_by — enforced in the Python cross-field layer only (`_cf_spinoff_roadmap_requires_graph`), NOT in this file's allOf; relaxing the one did not weaken the other. roadmap_id remains genuinely roadmap-scoped and still rejects on other kinds.)

blocked_by.description: Stub IDs OR handoff_id values that block this stub (namespace decision already made — do not re-open: the mutating path already matches blocker_id in (stub_id, handoff_id), so the compute index accepting both here makes it agree with what mutation already does). Permitted on ANY kind as of C1 — the former roadmap-only cross-field gate was removed so the gate resolver can carry non-roadmap batons, and `ops/handoff_children.blocked_by_dependents` plus the d6 roadmap-baton-decline evidence text both read it on non-baton handoffs. (kind=roadmap-baton still REQUIRES this field, along with roadmap_id/stub_id/wave/blocks — enforced in the Python cross-field layer only (`_cf_spinoff_roadmap_requires_graph`, whose required list names blocked_by explicitly), NOT in this file's allOf, so a schema-only reader is not misled; relaxing the one did not weaken the other. roadmap_id remains genuinely roadmap-scoped and still rejects on other kinds — `_cf_graph_fields_roadmap_only`, whose gated set is roadmap_id ALONE.) Pattern is deliberately permissive (no whitespace, no path separator, no .md extension) rather than fit to the numeric stub_id families (<slug>-<N>) — live records include shapes like pacl-05-a, strang-10-C, strang-10-inject-anchor, cis-producer-locator that a narrower `^[a-z]+-\d{2}$`-style pattern would reject outright.

roadmap_id.description: Roadmap identifier. Roadmap-only (kind=roadmap-baton); cross-field rule rejects on other kinds.

stub_id.description: Globally-unique stub code (<slug>-<N>). Required by cross-field rule when kind=roadmap-baton.

wave.description: Serialization-order grouping within a sprint. Required by cross-field rule when kind=roadmap-baton.

cost.description: Estimation tier T0|T1|T2|T3. Cross-field rule enforces allowed values when present.

suggested_priority.description: Advisory execution-priority signal an EM may attach to this handoff at authoring time. Optional (not nullable — absence already covers 'no suggestion'; a redundant null representation was reviewed out, see Finding 4 / review-integrator 2026-07-27). Enum is the priority-ledger domain (priority-ledger.schema.json's urgent|high|medium|low|none) MINUS 'none' — an EM has no reason to author an explicit clear; absence of the field already covers that case. Advisory only: the PM-owned priority ledger (state/priority-ledger/) is the authoritative tier and lives on a deliberately separate surface — this field never overrides it, and that separation (not memory) is what keeps 'advisory never overrides authoritative' structural. Do NOT add a pm_priority field to this frontmatter to compensate; the tier split is the point. NEGATIVE-SPEC: no inherited_from / priority_predecessor field is permitted on this frontmatter either — priority does not chain hop-to-hop the way carry_id does. No backfill of pre-existing handoffs, consistent with this schema's origin_* no-backfill policy.

category.description: Workstream category. Required by cross-field rule for handoffs created >= 2026-05-29. 'uncategorized' is the null-object sentinel for the one-time backfill normalizer only. 'queue-derived-baton' marks a handoff authored as a queue-triage terminus (solo or themed baton) rather than an ordinary session handoff — class-filterable per docs/plans/2026-07-23-queue-triage-terminates-in-batons.md; interim scaffolding uses 'infra' and hand-edits to this value until claude-klabauter's coordinator-doc-new default is updated (C9 memo). WIRE PROJECTION: this field is emitted into the cockpit contract as 'workstream_type' — same axis, two names, a 1:1 passthrough at claude-klabauter coordinator_core/ops/emit/sections/handoffs.py:401. Adding a value here is NOT sufficient on its own: the cockpit WorkstreamType Literal (coordinator_core/contract/cockpit_schema/entities/deliverable_spine.py) is a closed set and must gain the same value. A handoff carrying a value that Literal does not know is quarantined per-record into the emission's 'malformed' bucket with a logged reason (caught at emit/sections/handoffs.py:436-449) — the emission RUN still completes, but that baton vanishes from the wire and no fleet consumer can see or filter it. See docs/wiki/queue-terminus-doctrine.md § The cockpit projection.

summary.description: One-line session summary (<=140 chars). Required by cross-field rule for handoffs created >= 2026-05-29. Length enforced by cross-field rule.

reviewed_at_workstream_complete.description: Review marker written by /workstream-complete and /handoff. Format: '<sha-range> <reviewer> <YYYY-MM-DD>'. Absent on spinoff-kind handoffs.

completeness_checklist.description: Install/onboarding completeness items. Each item: '<class>: <assertion text> [probe: <shell-command>]'. Opt-in — intended for install/onboarding batons only.

supersedes.description: Conditional-live orientation-supersession field. Permitted only on kind=spinoff (cross-field rule enforced). Distinct from the terminal memo supersedes:/superseded_by: coupling.

additional_predecessors.description: Fan-in merge edges — additional parent handoff paths beyond the primary predecessor. Optional; requires explicit PM direction. Each entry is a path string to a predecessor handoff. Cross-field rules enforce: no duplicate entries within the array; no entry duplicating the primary predecessor field.

forked_from.description: Spinoff branch-point ancestry (lineage/render-only). Permitted only on kind=spinoff by cross-field kind-gate. NOT followed by the LoE aggregation primitive (DR-014 effort-isolation preserved); present for DAG rendering and lineage tracing only. Requires PM direction.

deliverable_id.description: Durable deliverable join key. Minted once at the earliest artifact (roadmap-spinoff stub or first plan/handoff) and carried verbatim by every downstream artifact. dlv-<stub_id> for roadmap-stub origins; dlv-<slug>-<6hex> for plan/handoff origins. Cross-field rule enforces 'dlv-' prefix when non-null. Null for pre-backfill artifacts. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-03-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets.md § D1

initiative.description: FK to the initiative entity (state/initiatives/<id>.yaml). Nullable — not all work belongs to a named initiative. Cross-field rule enforces non-empty string when non-null. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-03-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets.md § D2

caption.description: One-sentence business-legible outcome line. NOT an engineering title or filename — authored for CEO-board legibility (e.g. 'Shipped the Example-Fleet Pro billing flow'). Optional; authored at creation time.

status_reason.description: Free-text one-liner explaining the current status (e.g. 'abandoned — superseded by X'). Optional authored field; carried into the cockpit emission as a product-legibility facet.

owner.description: Authoring workstream or EM identifier. Nullable; carried forward from the earliest artifact for the deliverable.

origin_session.description: Originating-session provenance — the session UUID in which this fork was spawned. DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine, always none for forks), forked_from (branch-point ancestry, handoff-path), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Scalar 0..1. Id format: global UUID, no prefix (already globally unique). Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-07-spinoff-provenance-ancestry.md § Field shape

origin_handoff.description: Originating-handoff provenance — the active baton path (state/handoffs/…) at fork-authoring time. DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine), forked_from (branch-point ancestry, also a handoff-path but lineage/render-only), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Scalar 0..1. Id format: state/handoffs/… path (inherently namespaced). This is the sole origin_* field that is a handoff-DAG edge (registered in walk-handoff-dag.js EDGE_KIND_META); the other three are cross-entity refs. Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-07-spinoff-provenance-ancestry.md § Field shape

origin_handoff_id.description: ID-companion for origin_handoff (C2, add-not-swap) — the originating baton's handoff_id, resolved and stamped at author time from the SAME baton origin_handoff names (never a different one). Path-independent, survives the originating baton's archival/rename; origin_handoff remains the human-legible display path. Null when the originating baton has no handoff_id (pre-existing artifact, no backfill) or origin_handoff is null. Never-silently-disagree cross-field rule (origin_handoff/origin_handoff_id must resolve to the same artifact when both non-null) is owned by C3, not this schema file. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-08-lifecycle-vocab-c2-durable-links-rollup.md § C2

origin_plan_id.description: Originating-plan provenance — the plan under execution when this fork was spawned. DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine), forked_from (branch-point ancestry), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Scalar 0..1. Id format: pln-prefixed (e.g. pln-structured-originating-session-8b505c). Cross-entity ref — NOT a handoff-DAG edge; rag's origin_edges projection owns the durable query surface. Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-07-spinoff-provenance-ancestry.md § Field shape

origin_goal_id.description: Originating-goal provenance — the goal(s) tagged at fork-authoring time. Array (string[] | null) because multi-goal forks are real (a roadmap serving multiple goals; many-to-many InitiativeSummary.goals[]). DISTINCT from predecessor (continuation spine), forked_from (branch-point ancestry), and deliverable_id (dlv- grouping key). Each entry is goal-prefixed kebab-case (e.g. goal-shipping-velocity) — matches the goal.schema.json id field scheme. Cross-entity ref — NOT a handoff-DAG edge; rag's origin_edges projection fans array entries into N edge rows. Backfill=null for pre-existing forks; no migration. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-07-spinoff-provenance-ancestry.md § Field shape

handoff_id.description: Durable stable ID for this handoff/spinoff record, path-independent (survives archival move/rename). Minted via coordinator-doc-new's _mint_artifact_id(prefix="hnd", slug) at scaffold time — hnd-<slug>-<6hex>. OPTIONAL on new records going forward, but POLICY REVERSED 2026-07-27 (DR-102, C10) for the live corpus: state/handoffs/*.md records that predated this field were BACKFILLED via coordinator/lib/backfill-handoff-id.py (idempotent; frontmatter-primitives seam) — this supersedes the prior no-backfill prose, which was consistent with this schema's origin_* no-migration policy but is no longer accurate for handoff_id itself. archive/handoffs/ remains grandfathered (out of scope for the reversal), matching DR-096 §5's precedent for shipped_in on archived batons. This is the join key C2's predecessor_id/origin_handoff_id ID-companion ancestry fields resolve against — backfilling it serves LINEAGE tracking only and does NOT de-collide the gate index (which joins on id/stub_id, a separate namespace). Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-08-lifecycle-vocab-c2-durable-links-rollup.md § C1; DR-102

recovers_session.description: recovery-kind only: session-id of the crashed session being reconstructed. OPTIONAL, no cross-field enforcement (yet) — a future cross-field rule could require this to be non-null when kind=recovery, but that gate is left as a follow-up (see bin/lib/schema.js CROSS_FIELD_RULES['handoff'] comment).

handoff_phase.description: The plan→execute seam axis on kind: session-handoff AND canonical kind: roadmap-baton — it is NOT session-handoff-only. Absence ≡ continuation (going-forward default). OPTIONAL. The kind-gate MUST resolve the roadmap side through kind_values_for_canonical('roadmap-baton'), never a bare kind == 'roadmap-baton' literal: that canonical resolves to {roadmap-baton, spinoff-roadmap}, and real roadmap batons on disk carry kind: spinoff-roadmap — a literal gate would never fire on them. Admitting this field on roadmap-baton is NOT backfilling it — widening this validation gate does not widen any stamping predicate. Cross-field rules (stamp-required-when-execution: _cf_execution_stamp_required; kind-gate: _cf_handoff_phase_kind_gate) live in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-17-execution-handoff-phase-doe-contract.md § C1

execution_authorized_by.description: The PM/session that authorized execution. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note); required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-17-execution-handoff-phase-doe-contract.md § C1

execution_authorized_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of authorization. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note); required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-17-execution-handoff-phase-doe-contract.md § C1

execution_authorized_sha.description: git-hash-object of the plan body at authorization (the content-binding witness /pickup recomputes; schema shape-only). OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note); required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-17-execution-handoff-phase-doe-contract.md § C1

execution_authorized_note.description: The verbatim PM utterance that named execution. The FOURTH field of the stamp: plan-execute-session-split.md § Pinned conventions pins the stamp as a byte-identical FOUR-field contract (by/at/sha/note); note is the self-attesting field — a stamp without a note that names execution signals the write-bar may not have been met. Do NOT drop it. OPTIONAL — required-together enforcement (_cf_execution_stamp_required) lives in claude-klabauter/coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py's _HANDOFF_CROSS_FIELD_RULES list when handoff_phase=execution. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-17-execution-handoff-phase-doe-contract.md § C1

carry_id.description: Stable identity for one carried item, minted ONCE (cf-<slug>-<6hex>) the first time the item is carried, then threaded byte-identical through every successor handoff regardless of how the item's prose is re-worded hop to hop. This is the anti-evasion tooth: the gate (coordinator_core.ops.handoff_carry_gate, claude-klabauter) keys on carry_id, never on description text, so re-wording an item never resets its count. A new item (first appearance) mints a fresh carry_id at carry_count=1; an item continuing from the predecessor keeps its predecessor's carry_id and increments carry_count by exactly 1.

description.description: Human-readable one-liner for the item — free to reword hop to hop; carry_id (not this text) is the identity key.

carry_count.description: Number of consecutive handoffs (including this one) this item has been carried, keyed on carry_id. Increments by exactly 1 per hop relative to the predecessor's value for the same carry_id; a first appearance is carry_count: 1. Never hand-decremented — the gate treats a decrease as a malformed/ambiguous count and fails loud rather than silently allowing the carry (see handoff_carry_gate.evaluate_gate).

disposition.description: carried = still open, no sanctioned exit yet — ONLY legal while carry_count < 3 (coordinator_core.ops.handoff_carry_gate refuses to emit a carried-disposition item at carry_count >= 3: the third-carry gate). closed = terminated in place (disposition_detail names why, mirrors deployment_state: closed's closed_reason vocabulary). spun_off = forked into its own baton (disposition_detail names the spinoff handoff path/id). blocked = the sanctioned exit for a genuine external dependency (e.g. hardware-gated Windows-host validation) — remains visible and explicit rather than silently re-carried; disposition_detail must name the concrete blocking condition, not restate 'blocked'.

disposition_detail.description: Required whenever disposition != carried (cross-field rule _cf_carried_items_shape in coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py, claude-klabauter) — names the closure reason, the spinoff target, or the concrete external blocker. A disposition of closed/spun_off/blocked with no disposition_detail is the exact 'operator remembers' shape this field exists to eliminate, so the rule rejects it.

first_seen_handoff_id.description: handoff_id of the handoff where this carry_id was first minted (carry_count: 1). Null when unknown (pre-existing item backfilled without history). Provenance only — not consulted by the gate, which reads carry_count directly.

carried_items.description: Machine-readable replacement for the free-prose '_(carried via N handoffs)_' annotation under `## Carried Forward` — see coordinator/skills/handoff/SKILL.md § Cascading unresolved items. Each entry's carry_count is gate-checked by coordinator_core.ops.handoff_carry_gate (claude-klabauter) before the handoff is written: a disposition: carried entry at carry_count >= 3 is refused, forcing the item to be closed, spun off, or explicitly (and visibly) marked blocked instead of silently re-carried a fourth time.
